relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a woman with a diagnosis of PAPA syndrome: "A 66‐year‐old female with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and PAPA syndrome"; no PSTPIP1 variant is printed or attributed to her.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and checked spans. One in-scope person (diagnosis of PAPA syndrome), labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No variants table rows: the paper mentions PSTPIP1 only in the Introduction as the disease gene and never states that this patient was tested or carries a PSTPIP1 variant, so no variant is tied to her. n_patients_reported left null because the field counts patients with a PSTPIP1 variant and none is stated. Age 66 years is the age at presentation to the authors' center; recorded as age at last evaluation (time of report); later follow-up is given only by month. Pyoderma gangrenosum is hedged in the paper ('concerning for developing PG', 'consistent with PG', 'a course more characteristic of PG'); recorded as observed with the hedge kept in severity_or_detail. Rheumatoid arthritis counted toward the checklist item 'pyogenic sterile arthritis or other arthritis'. 'Recurrent periprosthetic infection' (abstract) counted toward the checklist item 'recurrent infections'; the pretibial abscess was culture-positive (Streptococcus mitis) but is still a soft-tissue abscess. 'No systemic signs of infection' recorded as excluded systemic signs of infection only; fever left not reported (a broader statement does not name fever). Postoperative bleeding requiring transfusion does not state anemia; anemia left not reported. No contradictions found.
